newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet to get 1997/98 budget hike request.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet to get 1997/98 budget hike request.

text.p: Thailand's Budget Bureau said on Wednesday it and the Finance Ministry would ask the cabinet to endorse a nine percent increase in the national budget for fiscal 1997/98.

Budget bureau director Seree Sukstaporn told reporters the cabinet would be asked to review a proposed 1,008 billion baht ($38.8 billion) 1997/98 (Oct-Sept) budget, up from 925 billion baht in 1996/97.
The budget for 1996/97 was trimmed from 984 billion after the government decided earlier this year to rein in unnecessary expenditure during the current economic slowdown.
Seree said Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh had been briefed informally of the planned budget increase last Friday.
The weekly cabinet meeting, usually held on Tuesday, is expected to be held on Thursday because of the traditional Thai New Year holidays from Monday to Wednesday.
In February, a government spokesman citing similar figures given by Seree said the cabinet had plans to adopt such a budget but no action was taken then.
Seree said the government would try to adopt another deficit-free balanced budget next year.
The official said it was premature to predict whether Thailand's slowing economy would prevent the government from meeting its tax revenue target. He did not elaborate.
